hook.text: Coastal dunes are the last defense between the ocean and the land—natural sea walls made of sand.

buildup.text: Wind blows dry sand inland from the beach—plants trap it, building dunes that grow over decades.

discovery.text: Dune grasses like marram have deep roots and grow through burial—they build dunes by catching sand.

twist.text: Without vegetation, dunes erode quickly—walking paths and development can destroy them in years.

climax.text: Well-maintained dunes absorb storm surge energy, protecting communities far more cheaply than sea walls.

punchline.text: A grass-covered sand hill can outlast a concrete wall.

quiz.question: How do coastal dunes form?
options: Wind carries sand inland, and vegetation traps it
